newsitem.title: FINLAND: KEY FINNISH CEN BANK BILL RULING NOT BEFORE APR 17.
newsitem.headline: KEY FINNISH CEN BANK BILL RULING NOT BEFORE APR 17.

text.p: Parliament's constitutional committee will rule by April 17 at the earliest on what kind of majority shall be needed to enact new Bank of Finland legislation, an official close to the committee said on Friday.

The committee had been expected to complete its task by end-March, but now the timetable pointed to a ruling -- in the form of a statement to the legislature's economic committee -- early in the second half of April, the official told Reuters by telephone.
"It could be April 17, that is probably the earliest possible date," he said.
The committee's decision, which cannot be overruled, is crucial for the government's drive to adapt Bank of Finland legislation to the requirements of a European Central Bank (ECB).
European economic and monetary union (EMU) requires EU countries to grant their central banks independence before the planned start of ECB operations in the summer of 1998.

If the constitutional committee rules that the reform of Finland's central bank legislation requires a qualified majority to become law, the left-right-green coalition may have trouble getting two-thirds of MPs to suppport the bill.
The five cabinet parties have 142 MPs in the 200-seat house where the speaker does not vote and so may need 133 votes to be assured of victory.
In a February 28 vote of confidence, 17 coalition party MPs voted against the government.

The most controversial proposed item in the central bank reform package is a transfer of all monetary and exchange rate policy decisions to the Bank's board of management, depriving the parliamentary supervisors of their minor but key role.

Opposition MPs and some MPs from governing parties have said the bill would remove political influence over monetary policy decisions, and some have claimed its sole purpose is to make sure that Finland qualifies for the third stage of EMU.
Plenary debate and voting on the Bank of Finland reform is due late in spring. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
